## Protocol

Precommitted before this sample was scored:

- Sample: first SPY session on or after 2000-01-03 through the last available session. The SMA may use earlier history. The T-bill input is the 13-week yield (`^IRX`), lagged one session, divided by 100 and by 252.
- Execution: the signal is fixed at the close and filled at the next open. Cash earns the lagged T-bill. SPY, SSO, and UPRO pay 5 bps one-way. Cash does not pay a spread in the base case.
- Leveraged sleeve: daily reset, `r_L = L * r - (L - 1) * (rf + 0.40% / 252) - ER / 252`, with expense ratios 0.89% (SSO) and 0.91% (UPRO). The synthetic open gaps by L times the underlying overnight move. Financing and the expense ratio sit in the rest of the close-to-close return.
- Grid, and every cell is a trial: leverage 2 and 3; sleeve weight 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70 percent; filters SMA 200 daily, SMA 200 daily with a 2% band, SMA 200 evaluated monthly, SMA 150 daily, and SMA 100 daily with a 2% band; mix reset monthly and quarterly. Plus a 100% sleeve for leverage 2 and 3 (the mix reset does nothing when the core weight is zero, so it is stored once). Plus unlevered sleeves of 50% and 100% on the same filters, monthly and quarterly.
- The desk's 50/50 UPRO mix is one of those cells: SMA 200, a 2% hysteresis band (enter when the close is above 1.02 times the average, exit only when it is below 0.98 times, hold the previous state in between), daily filter, quarterly mix. The desk chose that weight after seeing results. This study reports the cell as pre-specified. It does not crown it from the full-sample Sharpe.
- Walk-forward: on the first session of each year from 2006, pick the cell with the highest excess Sharpe versus T-bills using only returns strictly before that session, requiring 756 prior sessions. Ties break alphabetically. The stitched path is the out-of-sample record. It is compared with SPY over those same sessions, not with SPY from 2000.
- The live trend-core book is that 50/50 cell plus a dip overlay on the SPY half only. After three strictly down SPY closes, that half is SSO instead of SPY until the next open after the first up close or the fifth session, whichever comes first. The UPRO half is not resized by the dip. The other dip rules (two-day -2%, two-day -3%, three-day -3%, three-day -4%) are the same overlay on the same 50/50 book, and each rule is a trial.
- Buy-and-hold synthetic SSO and UPRO are trials. Buy-and-hold SPY is the benchmark and is not a trial. Cost and next-close reruns are recorded as audits and do not increment N.
- The walk-forward edge survives only if its CAGR exceeds buy-and-hold SPY over the same sessions (first decision date through the sample end), its information-ratio t-stat exceeds the expected maximum of N independent standard normals, and its deflated Sharpe ratio is at least 0.95. N and the Sharpe dispersion come from the persistent ledger.
- If that bar is cleared, the live book is the variant selected for the current year. If the path beats SPY but misses the bar, the edge does not survive; the flagship file still shows the rule's current weights and is marked not endorsed. If the path does not beat SPY, the recommendation is 100% SPY.
caveats: Synthetic 3x/2x returns before the ETF listing are a model. The overlap table is the check. Real swap spreads, dividend treatment inside the fund, and creation/redemption can differ from `ER` plus 40 bps over T-bills.
The multiple-testing bar treats trials as independent. These variants share one market, so the bar is conservative and a miss is informative. A pass would be more fragile than the formula suggests.
The 50/50 weight was the desk's post-hoc choice. It is inside the grid so it is counted. It is not re-selected on the full sample.
Block bootstrap redraws historical daily returns. It does not invent a new regime, and it ignores taxes. Trend and dip exits are mostly short-term gains in a taxable account.

A consumer that rebalances to `weights` every session implements the daily-reset mix, not the quarterly drift. `trade` and `rebalance_mix` say when the lower-turnover book would actually trade. `signals.json` is the fixed trend-core book, including the dip overlay on the SPY half. The flagship file is written by the separate return-max study.
This is research on public prices. It is not a recommendation to buy leveraged ETFs.

iterations.title: Credit-spread sleeve hedge
iterations.hypothesis: The live book keeps the 3x sleeve on until SPY closes through its 200-day band. That lag is the weakness in the refreshed subperiod table: the trend-core book trails SPY in 2020 and again in 2022. A widening credit spread is a faster stress signal. When the 20-session change in the spread exceeds a precommitted threshold, move only the leveraged sleeve to T-bills. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. The sleeve goes back to UPRO when the trend is on and the 20-session widening is back at or below the threshold.

iterations.title: Risk-off bond or gold trend
iterations.hypothesis: The live book leaves the SPY half invested after the 200-day band has moved the UPRO sleeve to cash. That is why the credit-spread hedge, the volatility scale, the multi-lookback vote, and the trailing-peak stop left the out-of-sample max drawdown near -46.8%: the trough is the equity bear after the sleeve is already in cash. This test does not try another faster exit for UPRO. Once a diversifier's own average exists, a day when SPY's 200-day 2% band is off moves the whole book, core and sleeve, out of equities. The book holds the diversifier while that asset's filter is on, and T-bills while it is off. While SPY's band is on, the book is the unchanged trend core, including the three-down-close dip on the SPY half. Until the diversifier's average exists, the book stays that trend core, so the years before the ETF lists are not a separate cash-timing rule. Assets are GLD, IEF, and TLT, alphabetical, so a neighbor is one step on that list. Windows are 100 and 200 sessions. Bands are 0 and 2%, the same hysteresis as the equity filter, evaluated daily. A variant's walk-forward history starts the session after its filter first becomes ready. Earlier sessions are the trend core and do not count toward the 756-session minimum. Full-sample rows still include them. The walk-forward may also select the current book. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

iterations.title: N-day confirmation of the 200-day band
iterations.hypothesis: The live sleeve already uses a 2% hysteresis band: it turns on only when SPY closes above 1.02 times its 200-day average and turns off only when the close is below 0.98 times that average. That rule, and a 0% band, are already in the original grid. A single close through the band still flips the sleeve, and the new state then sticks until the other side of the band. Those one-session pierces are the whipsaw: the book pays the 5 bp UPRO cost and the leveraged overnight gap, then often sits in the new state through a reversal. This test does not rescore the 2% band by itself. It requires N consecutive closes beyond the band before the state changes. A close that is not beyond the band in the flip direction resets the count, and the previous state is kept until the count is met. Bands are 0.5%, 1%, 2%, and 3%. Confirmation counts are 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 sessions. The cell with a 2% band and 1 day is the live filter, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep the current book. Every other cell is a new trial. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. iterations.title: Off-trend core hold in T-bills
iterations.hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. The credit-spread hedge, the volatility scale, the multi-lookback vote, the trailing-peak stop, and the N-day band confirmation all tried to get the UPRO sleeve out of equities sooner. They left that trough in place: by the time the drawdown bottoms, the sleeve is already in T-bills and the loss that remains is the SPY half, which the 200-day band never turns off. The idle-diversifier test then moved that residual equity into GLD, IEF, or TLT. It was rejected, and those assets made the stitched drawdown worse. This test does not buy another risky asset and does not change the sleeve's entry rule. While the same 200-day 2% band is off, only a fraction of the core budget stays in SPY (or in SSO when the three-down-close dip is on). The rest of that budget earns T-bills, the same cash the sleeve already earns. Fractions are 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1. The prior write-up's session on 2026-11-05 is the same lag in miniature: SPY closed at 733.00 against a 200-day average of 727.39, inside the band, and the book stayed half UPRO. Rules that replaced the sleeve with T-bills on a faster stress signal (the volatility scale, a vote of several simple averages, an N-day confirmation of the same band, the credit-spread hedge, and the trailing-peak stop) were rejected: the cash stake also sat out the rebound. Moving the sleeve from UPRO to SPY on a shorter simple average was rejected on 2026-11-06. This test does not add a second filter, does not move the sleeve to SPY, and does not rescore those simple averages. The original grid already contains simple averages of 100, 150, and 200 sessions. It does not contain an exponential average. The exponential filter uses the same span's center of mass but puts more weight on the recent closes, so the average sits closer to the price and the lower band is crossed after a smaller decline. On the way back up the new closes dominate, so the re-entry does not wait for a block of old prices to leave a rectangular window. The hysteresis is the live one: on only above the average times one plus the band, off only below the average times one minus the band. Spans are 100, 150, and 200 sessions. Bands are 0 and 2%. The six cells are new trials. The current simple-average book is the walk-forward's option to keep the present rule and is not a new trial. The core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

iterations.hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. By the time that trough prints, the UPRO sleeve is already in T-bills and the loss that remains is the SPY half. Rules that sold that half (the off-trend core hold, the fast re-entry that still left the core in T-bills for most of the off-trend episode, and the yield-curve clock) cut the drawdown by more than 3 points and were rejected: the cash stake also sat out the rebound, and the CAGR give-up was larger than half a point. The idle bond or gold test then moved the whole book, core and sleeve, into GLD, IEF, or TLT when the 200-day band was off. It was rejected, and the stitched drawdown got worse. The failure those tests share is selling the SPY half. This test does not sell it. While the 200-day 2% band is on, the book is the unchanged trend core, including the three-down-close dip and the quarterly mix. While that band is off, the core stays in SPY, or in SSO when the dip is on. Only the sleeve, which the live book already holds in T-bills, is replaced. If the diversifier's own average exists and its filter is on, that sleeve holds the diversifier. If the filter is off, or the average does not exist yet, the sleeve stays in T-bills. Assets are GLD, IEF, and TLT, alphabetical. Windows are 100 and 200 sessions. Bands are 0 and 2%, the same hysteresis as the equity filter, evaluated daily. The twelve cells are new trials. The current book, which leaves the sleeve in T-bills, is the walk-forward's option to keep the present rule and is not a new trial. A variant's walk-forward history starts the session after its filter first becomes ready. Earlier sessions are the trend core and do not count toward the 756-session minimum.
